en: Now begins the twenty-first chapter: The Chapter on the Results of the House of Karma (the Tenth House).
Now, O Maitreya, listen to the truth concerning the nature of karma and its fruit as spoken by Brahmā, Garga, and others; I shall declare it before you.

If the lord of the tenth house is weak but is in its exaltation, its own Navamsha, or its own sign, the person born will be endowed with paternal happiness, renowned, and a performer of auspicious deeds. || 2 ||
If the lord of the tenth house is weak in strength, one should predict a deficiency in one's actions;
however, if Mars is situated in a quadrant or a trine, he performs sacrifices such as the Jyotiṣṭoma.
When the lord of the tenth house is conjoined with a benefic and likewise situated in a benefic house, there is always profit at the royal court and in trade; otherwise, it is the opposite.
If the tenth house is conjoined with malefic planets and the eleventh house is likewise associated with malefics,
a mortal man incurs ill-repute and becomes a reviler of his own kinsmen.
If the lord of the tenth house is situated in the eighth house and likewise conjoined with Rāhu,
the man becomes a hater of people, a great fool, and incurs evil deeds.
If the lord of the tenth house is situated in the seventh house and is conjoined with Saturn and Mars,
and the lord of the seventh house is associated with malefic planets, the native will be devoted to his genitals and belly.
If the lord of the tenth house is conjoined with Jupiter and is situated in the sign of Leo (Tuṅga),
and the lord of the ninth house is situated in the tenth house, one will possess honor, sovereignty, and prowess.

If the lord of the eleventh house is situated in the tenth house and the lord of the tenth house is conjoined with the ascendant, or if both of them are placed in a quadrant (kendras), one shall enjoy a happy livelihood. || 9 ||

When the lord of the tenth house is endowed with strength and is situated in Pisces conjoined with Jupiter, one obtains clothing, ornaments, happiness, and so forth; of this there is no doubt. || 10 ||
If the Sun is situated in the house of gain (the eleventh house) and is conjoined with Rāhu and Mars,
or associated with Saturn, the man will become a supervisor of works.

If Jupiter is in Pisces conjoined with Venus, and the lord of the ascendant is endowed with strength while the Moon is situated in its own exaltation sign, one will possess perfect knowledge and wealth. (12)

When the lord of the ascendant is situated in the house of gain, the lord of the house of gain is situated in the ascendant, and Venus is situated in the house of action (the tenth house), that man shall possess jewels. 13.
If the lord of the tenth house is situated in a quadrant or a trine, occupying its own exaltation,
and is conjoined with or aspected by Jupiter, that person shall be endowed with success in his actions.

If the lord of the tenth house is situated in the ascendant and is conjoined with the lord of the ascendant, and the Moon is placed in a quadrant or a trine, one becomes devoted to virtuous deeds. || 15 ||
If Saturn is situated in the tenth house and conjoined with a base planet,
and the tenth-part (karmāṃśa) is joined by malefic planets, a man will be devoid of action (or livelihood).

If the lord of the tenth house is situated in the eighth house and the lord of the eighth house is situated in the tenth house, and both are conjoined with a malefic planet, one becomes devoted to evil deeds. || 17 ||
If the lord of the tenth house is in its sign of debilitation, or if a malefic planet is situated in the tenth house, or if a malefic is placed in the tenth from the tenth house,
one should predict a deficiency in one's professional or karmic activities.
When the Moon is situated in the tenth house, its lord is in a trine from it, and the lord of the ascendant is placed in a quadrant, one shall be endowed with good fame. (19)

If the lord of the eleventh house is situated in the tenth house and the lord of the tenth house is endowed with strength, and [the latter] is aspected by Jupiter (the preceptor of the gods), one will be possessed of good fame. || 20 ||
If the lord of the tenth house is in the ninth house and the lord of the ascendant is conjoined with the tenth,
and the Moon is in the fifth house from the ascendant, the man will become famous by name.
Thus, O best of the twice-born, the fruit of karma has been declared in brief;
other matters as well should be inferred by oneself from the relationship between the ascendant and the lord of the house of action. (22)
Now begins the chapter on the results of the house of gains (the eleventh house), Chapter 22.
Now, O best of the twice-born, I shall describe the results pertaining to the ninth house (the house of gain);
listen to how one born under such a configuration is always happy in this world.

When the lord of the eleventh house is situated in the eleventh house, in a quadrant, or in a trine, it then bestows abundant gain; this remains true even if it is in its exaltation or in a solar degree (sūryāṃśa). || 2 ||

If the lord of the eleventh house is situated in the second house and the lord of the second house is placed in a quadrant (kendram), conjoined with Jupiter, one should predict gain from a preceptor. || 3 ||
If the lord of the eleventh house is in the third house and conjoined with a benefic planet,
upon reaching the thirty-sixth year, one will possess two thousand niṣkas.
When the lord of the eleventh house is situated in a quadrant or a trine and is conjoined with benefics,
upon reaching the fortieth year, one becomes a possessor of five hundred gold coins.
If the eleventh house is conjoined with Jupiter, the second house is endowed with the Moon,
and Venus is situated in the ninth house, one becomes the lord of six thousand.
When Jupiter is in the second house from the ascendant and is conjoined with Mercury and the Moon,
one becomes a lord of wealth and grain, illustrious, and endowed with ornaments such as gems and the like.
When the lord of the eleventh house is situated in the ascendant and the lord of the ascendant is conjoined with the eleventh house,
and the thirty-third year arrives, one shall possess a share of a thousand niṣkas.
If the lord of the second house is situated in the eleventh house and the lord of the eleventh house is in the second house, one should predict great fortune after marriage. || 9 ||
When the lord of the third house is situated in the eleventh house and the lord of the eleventh house is situated in the third house,
there is the acquisition of wealth from siblings, and one is endowed with divine ornaments.
If the lord of the eleventh house is in its sign of debilitation, in its fall, or in a trine occupied by malefic planets,
there will never be any gain, even when great effort has been made.
Now begins the chapter on the results of the twelfth house (vyayabhāva), [chapter] 23.
Then he said: "O twice-born one, I shall now describe the results of the twelfth house (vyayabhāva).
When the lord of the twelfth house is conjoined with a benefic, or is situated in its own sign or its exaltation," || 1 ||
And when the twelfth house is conjoined with a benefic, there is then expenditure for virtuous deeds;
the Moon, as the lord of the twelfth house, is situated among the mantras for the acquisition of merit. || 2 ||

If [the Moon] is in its exaltation, its own sign, or its own Navamsha, or in the Navamshas of the eleventh, ninth, or fifth houses, one possesses a divine bed in a celestial mansion and enjoys exclusively divine perfumes. || 3 ||
Delighting in the most excellent pleasures, adorned with divine garments, garlands, and ornaments,
and endowed with the finest wealth, the wise lord passes his days.
Likewise, situated in its own enemy's Navāṃśa, its depression Navāṃśa, its eighth Navāṃśa, or in the eighth house from the enemy [sign], it makes the native devoid of happiness from his wife. || 5 ||
Exhausted by excessive expenditure and deprived of divine enjoyments,
he indeed remains stationed in a quadrant or a trine, yet is himself adorned by his own wife.
Just as this result from the ascendant has been proclaimed for oneself,
so too should one examine all those [results] in the houses of brothers and the rest.
Planets situated in the visible half of the zodiac bestow perceptible results;
planets situated in the invisible half are traditionally held to yield results that are imperceptible.
If Rāhu is situated in the house of expenditure (the twelfth house) conjoined with Mars, Saturn, and the Sun,
and its lord is also conjoined with the Sun, there will be a fall into hell.
If Mercury is situated in the twelfth house, its lord is in its own exaltation sign, and is joined with or aspected by benefics, there will be liberation; of this there is no doubt. || 10 ||
If the lord of the twelfth house is conjoined with a malefic, and the twelfth house itself is occupied by a malefic,
or aspected by a malefic planet, [the native] has gone from one country to another.
If the lord of the twelfth house is situated in a benefic sign, the twelfth house itself is conjoined with a benefic,
and is aspected by a benefic planet, there will be travel from one's own country.
When the twelfth house is conjoined with Saturn and the like, or occupied by Mars, there is no attainment through the sight of benefics; the acquisition of wealth arises from sinful sources.
When the lord of the ascendant is situated in the twelfth house and the lord of the twelfth house is conjoined with the ascendant and joined by Venus,
there is expenditure of wealth due to religious duties.
Now begins the twenty-fourth chapter: The Chapter on the Results of the Lord of the Ninth House.

If the lord of the ascendant is situated in the ascendant, the native will enjoy physical comfort, possess strength of arms and valor, be high-minded, fickle, have two wives, and may even be devoted to another's wife. || 1 ||
If the lord of the ascendant is in the second house, the native will be wealthy, learned, happy, virtuous, knowledgeable in dharma, honorable, and endowed with many wives and good qualities. || 2 ||
If the lord of the ascendant is in the third house, the native possesses prowess equal to that of a lion;
he is endowed with all prosperity, is honorable, has two wives, is intelligent, and is happy. (3)
If the lord of the ascendant is situated in the fourth house, the native will be endowed with happiness from father and mother;
he will have many brothers, be lustful, and be possessed of virtues and beauty. || 4 ||
If the lord of the ascendant is in the fifth house, the person will have mediocre happiness from children;
there will be the loss of the first-born child, and he will be proud, irascible, and dear to the king. || 5 ||
If the lord of the ascendant is situated in the sixth house, the person born is devoid of physical comfort;
if it is joined with malefic planets and bereft of the aspect of benefics, there is suffering from enemies.
If the lord of the ascendant is in the seventh house and is a malefic, his wife does not survive;
if it is a benefic, he will be either poor, or detached from worldly life, or even a king.
If the lord of the ascendant is in the eighth house, the native is an expert in accomplished sciences;
yet he is diseased, a thief, highly irascible, addicted to gambling, and a violator of others' wives. || 8 ||
If the lord of the ascendant is situated in the ninth house, the native will be fortunate, beloved by the people,
a devotee of Viṣṇu, eloquent, and endowed with a wife, sons, and wealth.

If the lord of the ascendant is in the tenth house, the native will be endowed with paternal happiness; he will be honored by kings, famous among people, and a possessor of wealth earned by his own efforts—of this there is no doubt. (10)
If the lord of the ascendant is in the eleventh house, the native is always endowed with gains;
he is of good character, renowned for his fame, and possessed of many wives and virtues. || 11 ||
If the lord of the ascendant is situated in the twelfth house and is devoid of auspicious aspects or yogas, the native will be deprived of physical comfort,
spend money in vain, and be prone to great anger.
If the Lord of the Second House (Dhaneśa) is situated in the Ascendant, the person born will possess sons and wealth;
he will be a thorn to his family, lustful, harsh, and a doer of others' work.
If the lord of the second house is situated in the second house, the person born becomes wealthy and full of pride;
he may have two wives or many wives, but he is born without sons.
If the Lord of Wealth (Venus) is in the third house, one born [therein] is valorous, intelligent, and virtuous;
he is lustful and greedy. If it is endowed with benefics, he is rich; if endowed with malefics, he is a reviler of the gods. || 15 ||
When the Lord of Wealth (Venus) is situated in the house of happiness (the fourth house), a man is endowed with all prosperity;
if it is conjoined with Jupiter and in its own exaltation, he becomes equal to a king.
When the lord of the second house is situated in the fifth house, the native is endowed with wealth;
moreover, his sons also become inclined toward the acquisition of wealth. (17)
If the lord of the second house is situated in the sixth house with a benefic, there is wealth from enemies;
if it is with a malefic, there is loss from enemies, and one may suffer from a deformity of the legs.
If the Lord of Wealth (Venus) is in the seventh house at birth, the native is devoted to the wives of others and becomes a physician;
if it is aspected by or joined with a malefic, his wife will be unchaste.
If the lord of the second house is in the eighth house at birth, the native will be endowed with abundant land and wealth;
however, his happiness from his wife will be meager, and he will have no happiness from his elder brother.
When the Lord of Wealth (Venus) is situated in the ninth house, the native will be wealthy, industrious, and clever;
he will be sickly in childhood but happy later on, and will perform pilgrimages, religious duties, vows, and so forth.
If the Lord of Wealth (Venus) is in the tenth house, the native is lustful, honorable, and learned;
he is endowed with great generosity and wealth, yet somewhat deprived of the happiness of sons. || 22 ||
When the Lord of Wealth (Venus) is situated in the eleventh house, the man becomes endowed with all gains;
he is diligent, honorable, and renowned. (23)
If the Lord of Wealth (Venus) is situated in the twelfth house, the native will be devoid of wealth;
he will be intent on the fortune of others and will not have happiness from his eldest child.
If the lord of the third house is in the ascendant, the native possesses wealth acquired by his own efforts;
he is skilled in service, courageous, and wise even though lacking formal learning. (25)
In the second house, if its lord is Sahaja (the Moon), the native will be stout but devoid of valor;
he will have few undertakings, will not be happy, and will be lustful after the wives and wealth of others. || 26 ||
When Sahaja is the lord of Sahaja, one is endowed with the happiness of siblings;
possessed of wealth and sons, being joyful, he enjoys wonderful happiness. (27)
If the lord of the fourth house is situated in the fourth house, the child becomes happy and endowed with wealth;
he is intelligent, yet he becomes the husband of a wicked wife.
If the lord of the third house is situated in the fifth house, one will have sons endowed with virtues;
however, his wife will be cruel if [the fifth house] is conjoined with or aspected by malefic planets.
If the lord of the third house is in the sixth house, the person will have brothers who are his enemies yet possess great wealth;
he will have enmity with his maternal uncles and will be dear to his mother's sisters.
If the lord of the fourth house is in the seventh house, the man will be devoted to royal service;
he will be miserable in childhood but happy at the end, of this there is no doubt. (31)
If the lord of the fourth house is in the eighth house,
the person born will be one who subsists by the service of others as a servant, and his death will occur at the royal gate.
If the lord of the ninth house is in the ninth house, he will be devoid of paternal happiness;
however, his fortune shall rise through women, and he will be endowed with the happiness of sons and other blessings.
If the lord of the fourth house is in the tenth, the native is endowed with all happiness,
possesses wealth earned by his own efforts, and is intent on supporting wicked women.
If the lord of the fourth house is in the eleventh house, one is always possessed of gains;
though lacking formal learning, he is intelligent, courageous, and a servant to others. (35)
If the lord of the third house is situated in the twelfth house, the person will have wicked kinsmen;
his father will be cruel, yet there will likewise be the rise of fortune through women.
If the lord of the fourth house is in the second house, the person born is adorned with learning and virtues;
he is endowed with land and vehicles and is possessed of happiness from his mother. || 37 ||
If the lord of the fourth house is in the second house, the person born will be an enjoyer endowed with all kinds of wealth;
he will be accompanied by his family, honorable, courageous, and possessed of guile. || 38 ||

If the lord of the fourth house is in the third house at birth, the native will be valiant, accompanied by servants, noble, free from disease, virtuous, charitable, and possessed of wealth earned by his own arms. (39)
If the lord of the fourth house is situated in the fourth house, the practitioner of mantra will be endowed with all wealth; he will be clever, virtuous, honorable, wise, beloved by women, and happy.
If the lord of the fourth house is situated in the fifth house, the native is happy, beloved by all people, a devotee of Viṣṇu, virtuous, honorable, and possesses wealth earned by his own arms. (41)
If the lord of the fourth house is situated in the sixth house, one is deprived of his mother's happiness;
he is prone to anger, a thief, a practitioner of malevolent magic, follows his own whims, and is dejected in mind. (42)

If the lord of the fourth house is in the seventh house at birth, the native will be endowed with many branches of knowledge; yet, having abandoned the wealth acquired by his father, he will become like one mute in the assembly.
If the lord of the fourth house is situated in the eighth house, the native will be deprived of happiness from home and other such comforts;
he will have little happiness from his parents and will be like a eunuch.
If the lord of the fourth house (Sukheśa) is situated in the ninth house (Bhāgyabhāva), the person born will be beloved by all people;
he will be a devotee of the gods, virtuous, honorable, and endowed with every happiness. || 45 ||
If the lord of the fourth house is situated in the tenth house, the man will be honored by the king;
he will be an alchemist, greatly joyful, an enjoyer of pleasures, and one who has conquered his senses.
If the lord of the fourth house is in the eleventh house at birth, the native is afflicted by the fear of secret diseases;
yet he is noble, virtuous, charitable, and devoted to helping others. || 47 ||
If the lord of the fourth house is situated in the twelfth house, the native is deprived of happiness from home and other comforts;
he is addicted to evil vices, foolish, and always possessed by laziness.
If the lord of the fifth house is situated in the ascendant at birth, the native will possess learning and be endowed with the happiness of sons;
yet he will be a miser, crooked-minded, and a stealer of others' wealth. (49)

If the lord of the fifth house is in the second house, the person born will have many sons, be endowed with wealth, support his family, be honorable, dear to his wife, and possess great fame on earth. (50)
If the lord of the fifth house is in the third house, one is born dear to siblings;
yet he is also a slanderer, miserly, and always intent upon his own affairs.

If the lord of the fifth house is situated in the fourth house, one is happy, endowed with maternal happiness, possessed of fortune and excellent intellect, and becomes either a minister or a preceptor to a king. (52)
If the fifth house is the lord of the fifth house and is enriched by benefics, the man will have sons;
if it is enriched by malefics, he will be childless, yet virtuous and affectionate toward friends. (53)
If the lord of the fifth house is situated in the sixth house, the son will be equal to an enemy;
or he may be born with a deceased offspring, or else he will be an adopted or purchased son. (54)
If the lord of the fifth house is in the seventh, the native is honorable, endowed with all virtues, possessed of happiness from sons and others, and devoted to helping others. || 55 ||
If the lord of the fifth house is situated in the eighth house, [the native] will possess very little happiness from children;
he will be afflicted by cough and asthma, prone to anger, and devoid of comfort. || 56 ||
If the lord of the fifth house is in the ninth house, there will be a son who is equal to the lord of the house;
or he himself will be the author of books, renowned, and the illuminator of his lineage. (57)
If the lord of the fifth house is situated in the ninth house, a royal yoga indeed arises;
the man shall be an enjoyer of manifold pleasures and shall possess renowned fame. (58)
If Venus is in the eleventh house, the person born is learned, beloved by the people, an author of books, highly capable, and endowed with many sons and wealth. || 59 ||
If the lord of the fifth house is situated in the twelfth house, the native is deprived of the happiness of having sons;
he may, however, be endowed with an adopted son or possessed of a purchased son.
If the lord of the sixth house is situated in the ascendant, the person born will be diseased yet endowed with fame;
he will be an enemy to himself, wealthy, honorable, daring, and virtuous.

If the lord of the sixth house is situated in the second house, the native will be daring, renowned in his family, a traveler to foreign lands, happy, eloquent, and always devoted to his own duties. 62.
If the lord of the sixth house is situated there, the native is born with siblings who are wrathful and devoid of valor;
his brother is like an enemy, and his servant is one who gives contrary answers. (63)
If the lord of the sixth house is situated in the fourth house, the native is deprived of his mother's happiness;
yet he is wise, malicious, hateful, fickle-minded, and possesses great wealth.
If the lord of the sixth house is situated in the fifth house, his wealth and other possessions are unstable;
he has enmity with sons and friends, yet he is happy, self-interested, and endowed with compassion.

If the lord of the sixth house is situated in the sixth house, there will be enmity with one's own circle of kinsmen, but friendship with others; there will be moderate happiness arising from wealth and other such sources. (66)
If the lord of the sixth house is situated in the seventh house, the native is devoid of happiness from his wife;
yet he is famous, virtuous, honorable, daring, and endowed with wealth. (67)
If the lord of the sixth house is in the eighth house, the person born will be diseased and an enemy to wise men;
he will covet the wealth of others, be devoted to the wives of others, and be impure.
If the lord of the sixth house is situated in the ninth house, the native becomes a seller of wood and stone; in his business dealings, there is loss at times and gain at others. (69)
If the lord of the sixth house is in the tenth house, the person will be renowned in his family, disrespectful toward his father, talkative, and happy in a foreign land. 70.
If the lord of the sixth house is in the eleventh house at birth, the native will obtain wealth from enemies;
he will be virtuous, daring, and honorable, yet devoid of the happiness of children. (71)
If the lord of the sixth house is situated in the twelfth house, the native will always be prone to vice and expenditure;
he will be a hater of the learned and intent upon the injury of living beings.
If the lord of the seventh house is situated in the ascendant, the person born will be a libertine with the wives of others;
he is wicked, clever, lacking in fortitude, and afflicted by diseases of the wind (vāta). || 73 ||
If the lord of the seventh house is in the second house at birth, the person will be endowed with many wives;
through the conjunction with the wife, there is acquisition of wealth, and the man is also characterized by procrastination.
If the lord of the seventh house is in the third house at birth, the person indeed has deceased offspring;
sometimes a daughter is born, and even a son lives only with great effort. (75)
If the lord of the seventh house is situated in the fourth house, his wife is never under his control;
he himself is fond of truth, intelligent, and righteous in nature, yet afflicted with dental disease.
If Mars is in the fifth house from the lord of the seventh, the person born therein is proud, endowed with all virtues, always filled with joy, and likewise a master of all wealth. || 77 ||
If the lord of the seventh house is situated in the sixth house, his wife will be afflicted by disease;
or else, he will have enmity with his wife, being himself prone to anger and deprived of happiness.
If the lord of the seventh house is in the seventh house, the native will be endowed with happiness from a wife;
he will be steadfast, discerning, and wise, though afflicted solely by wind-related diseases.
If the lord of the seventh house is situated in the eighth house, the native is deprived of the happiness of a wife;
his wife, moreover, is afflicted by disease, ill-behaved, and not devoted to him. (80)
When the lord of the seventh house is situated in the ninth house, there is union with various women;
the man becomes one whose mind is captivated by his wife and who undertakes many enterprises.
If the lord of the seventh house is situated in the tenth house, his wife does not remain submissive;
he himself is born devoted to righteousness and endowed with wealth, sons, and other blessings.
If the lord of the seventh house is situated in the eleventh house, there is acquisition of wealth through one's wife;
however, there will be little happiness from sons and other [offspring], and the person will have daughters as progeny. (83)
If the lord of the seventh house is situated in the twelfth house, the native will be poor or even miserly;
his wife as well will be profligate, and the man will live by means of clothing.
If the lord of the eighth house is in the first house, the native is devoid of physical comfort;
he is a reviler of gods and Brahmins and is afflicted with wounds. (85)
If the lord of the eighth house is in the second house, one is born deficient in physical strength;
his wealth will be meager, and lost property will not be recovered. (86)
If the lord of the eighth house is in the third house, there is no happiness from brothers;
he becomes lazy, devoid of servants, and bereft of strength. (87)
If the lord of the eighth house is situated in the fourth house, the child will be deprived of his mother;
he will be destitute of home, land, and comforts, and will be a betrayer of friends—of this there is no doubt. (88)
If the lord of the eighth house is situated in the fifth house, one born [therein] becomes dull-witted;
however, he will possess little wisdom, yet be long-lived and endowed with wealth. (89)
If the lord of the eighth house is situated in the sixth house, a person will be a conqueror of enemies;
however, his body will be afflicted by disease, and there will be fear of snakes and water during childhood. (90)
If the lord of the eighth house is situated in the seventh house, the native shall have two wives;
furthermore, if that [lord] is joined with a malefic, loss in business will certainly occur.
If the lord of the eighth house is situated in the eighth house, the native will be endowed with a long life;
if it is weak, there will be a middling lifespan, and he will be a thief, contemptible, and a reviler of others. 92.
If the lord of the eighth house is situated in the ninth house, he is a hater of righteousness, an atheist, a husband of a wicked wife, and a stealer of others' property. || 93 ||
If the lord of the eighth house is in the tenth house, one is deprived of paternal happiness;
he is malicious and devoid of action, provided it is not aspected by a benefic.
If the lord of the eighth house is situated in the eleventh house with a malefic, one is devoid of wealth;
if it is conjoined with a benefic, one is miserable in childhood but happy later on and long-lived. (95)
If the lord of the eighth house is situated in the twelfth house, it always causes expenditure on evil deeds;
the native born will be short-lived, especially if [the lord] is associated with a malefic. || 96 ||
If the lord of the ninth house is situated in the ascendant, the person born will be fortunate, honored by kings, virtuous, handsome, learned, and revered by the people. (97)
When the lord of the ninth house is situated in the second house, one becomes learned, beloved by people, wealthy, lustful, and endowed with the happiness of wife, sons, and so forth. || 98 ||
If the lord of the ninth house is situated in the third house, the person born will be endowed with happiness from brothers;
he will also be wealthy, virtuous, and possessed of beauty and good character. || 99 ||
When the lord of the ninth house is situated in the fourth house, a man will be endowed with the comforts of home and vehicles, possessed of all prosperity, and devoted to his mother. (100)
When the lord of the ninth house (the Bhāgyeśa) is situated in the fifth house, the man is endowed with children and fortune;
he is devoted to his teacher, steadfast, righteous-souled, and learned.
If the lord of the ninth house is situated in the sixth house, the man will have little fortune;
he will be deprived of the happiness derived from maternal uncles and others, and will be constantly oppressed by enemies. (102)
If the lord of the ninth house is situated in the seventh house, there is the arising of happiness through marriage;
moreover, O best of the twice-born, he becomes virtuous and renowned. (103)
If the lord of the ninth house is situated in the eighth house, the person born will be devoid of fortune;
he shall never experience happiness from his elder brother. (104)
If the lord of the ninth house is situated in the ninth house, one is endowed with great fortune,
possessed of virtues and beauty, and has much happiness from siblings.
If the lord of the ninth house is situated in the tenth house, the native becomes a king or one equal to him;
or else he becomes a minister or a commander-in-chief, virtuous and honored by the people. (106)
If the lord of the ninth house is situated in the eleventh house, there is gain of wealth day after day;
he is devoted to his elders, virtuous, and meritorious as well. (107)
If the lord of the ninth house is situated in the twelfth house, it causes the loss of fortune for men;
there is constant expenditure on auspicious deeds, and one becomes impoverished due to the company of guests.
If the lord of the tenth house is situated in the ascendant at birth, the native will be learned, famous, wealthy, and a poet;
he will be sickly in childhood but happy thereafter, with his wealth increasing day by day. (109)

If the lord of the tenth house is situated in the second house, one becomes wealthy, endowed with virtues, honored by the king, generous, and possessed of happiness from one's father and others. || 110 ||
If the lord of the tenth house is situated in the third house at birth, the man will be endowed with happiness from brothers and servants;
he will be valiant, possessed of good qualities, eloquent, and devoted to truth. || 111 ||
If the lord of the tenth house (Karmeśa) is situated in the fourth house, the native is happy, devoted to his mother, a master of vehicles, land, and houses, and is both virtuous and wealthy. 112.
When the lord of the tenth house is situated in the fifth house, one is endowed with all branches of knowledge;
he is always filled with joy, wealthy, and possessed of sons. (113)
If the lord of the tenth house is situated in the sixth house, one is deprived of paternal happiness;
even if clever, he is destitute of wealth and oppressed by enemies. (114)
If Rājyeśa is situated in the house of the wife (the seventh house), the person born will be endowed with the happiness of a spouse;
he will be high-minded, virtuous, eloquent, and always devoted to truth and righteousness. || 115 ||
If the lord of the tenth house is situated in the eighth house, a man will be devoid of action;
even if he is born long-lived, he will be devoted to censuring others.
If one is born in the Bhāgya-bha (the ninth house) from the ruler of the ascendant, he becomes a king born of a royal lineage;
or, if born in another family, he becomes equal to such a king, endowed with wealth, sons, and other blessings. || 117 ||
When the lord of the tenth house is situated in the ninth house, the man becomes proficient in all actions, happy, valiant, truthful in speech, and devoted to his guru. (118)
If Rājyeśa is situated in the house of gain (the eleventh house), the native will be endowed with wealth and sons;
he will be joyful, virtuous, truthful in speech, and always happy. (119)
If the lord of the tenth house is situated in the twelfth house, there will be expenditure in the royal palace;
he will constantly face fear from enemies and will be troubled by his own intellect. (120)
If the lord of the eleventh house is situated in the ascendant, the native is virtuous, wealthy, and happy;
he possesses impartial vision, is a poet, eloquent, and is always endowed with gains. (121)
If the lord of the eleventh house is situated in the second house, the native is endowed with all wealth;
he possesses every accomplishment, is charitable, righteous, and always happy. (122)

If the lord of the eleventh house is situated in the third house, the native is skilled in all undertakings, wealthy, endowed with happiness from brothers, and may occasionally face fear of abdominal pain (śūla). 123.
If the lord of the eleventh house is situated in the fourth house, there will be gain from the mother's family;
the native will undertake pilgrimages and be endowed with the happiness of home and land. (124)
If the lord of the eleventh house is situated in the fifth house, one's sons will be happy, learned, and of virtuous character;
moreover, the person himself will be devoted to dharma and happy.
If the lord of the eleventh house is situated in the sixth house, the native is afflicted by disease;
he possesses a cruel intellect, is a wanderer, and is tormented by enemies. || 126 ||
If the lord of the eleventh house is situated in the seventh house, there is always gain from the wife's family;
the person is noble, virtuous, and lustful, and remains subservient to his wife.
If the lord of the eleventh house is situated in the eighth house, loss occurs in one's undertakings;
his lifespan will be long, yet death shall first come from a woman. 128.
If the lord of the tenth house is situated in the ninth house, the man becomes fortunate;
he is clever, truthful, honored by kings, and a master of wealth. || 129 ||
If the lord of the eleventh house is situated in the tenth house, one is honored by kings, endowed with virtues, devoted to one's own duty, intelligent, truthful, and a master of the senses. (130)
If the lord of the eleventh house is situated in the eleventh house, there is gain in all undertakings;
his scholarship and happiness increase day by day. (131)
If the lord of the eleventh house is situated in the twelfth house, there is constant expenditure on good works;
[the native] is lustful, has many wives, and associates with barbarians (mlecchas). 132.
If the lord of the twelfth house is situated in the ascendant at birth, the person born will be profligate, weak, afflicted by phlegmatic diseases, and devoid of wealth and learning. (133)
If the lord of the twelfth house is situated in the second house, there is always expenditure for auspicious deeds;
[the native] is righteous, pleasant-spoken, and endowed with virtues and happiness.
If the lord of the twelfth house is situated in the third house at birth, the native will be devoid of brotherly affection;
he will be hostile toward other people and solely intent on nourishing his own body. (135)
If the lord of the twelfth house is situated in the fourth house, the native is deprived of happiness from his mother;
furthermore, there is a daily loss of land, vehicles, houses, and so forth. 136.
If the lord of the twelfth house is situated in the fifth house, the person is devoid of children and learning;
he spends his wealth on the sake of sons and is intent upon wandering to holy places.
If the lord of the twelfth house is situated in the sixth house, the man born will be one who creates enmity with his own kin, wrathful, sinful, miserable, and devoted to the wives of others. (138)
If the lord of the twelfth house is situated in the seventh house, there is constant expenditure caused by the wife;
he possesses no happiness from his spouse and is devoid of strength and learning. (139)
If the lord of the twelfth house is situated in the eighth house, the native will always be endowed with gains;
he will be pleasant of speech, possess middling longevity, and be possessed of complete virtues. || 140 ||
If the lord of the twelfth house is situated in the ninth house, the man will be a hater of his teacher;
he will have enmity even with his friends and will be intent on achieving his own selfish ends. 141.
If the lord of the twelfth house is situated in the ninth house, expenditure will arise from the royal family;
indeed, his happiness derived from his father will be very slight. (142)
If the lord of the twelfth house is situated in the eleventh house, loss occurs regarding gains;
however, the man may occasionally obtain wealth protected by another.
If the lord of the twelfth house is situated in the twelfth house, there is indeed an excess of expenditure;
he finds no physical comfort and is prone to anger and hatred toward men. (144)
Thus, O Brahmin, I have told you the fruit of the Bhāvas and Īśas;
one should determine the result of all of them by discerning their relative strength and weakness. || 145 ||
Having understood the results in both ways for a planet that rules two signs, when two [planets] have equal opposing results, their destruction occurs. (146)
When two distinct results are present, the attainment of both will certainly occur;
however, when a planet possesses full strength, the result is full, and when it possesses half-strength, the result is half. (147)

When a planet is weak in strength, it should be understood by the wise that its value is one-quarter; thus have I stated the *pala* values for the lords of the houses situated in their respective houses. (148)
Now begins the twenty-fifth chapter on the results of planetary aspects when not in conjunction.
I have declared the results of the houses for the seven planets beginning with the Sun;
now I shall describe the results of the non-luminous planets. || 1 ||
A man who has the sign named Dhūma situated in the Mūrti house is always brave, possesses the luster of pure eyes, is stubborn, merciless, and wicked, and is ever possessed of intense anger.
When the second Dhumā stage is reached, one becomes diseased, wealthy yet deficient in limbs, with a mind robbed of its sovereignty, dull-witted, and a eunuch. || 3 ||
When Dhūma is situated in its natural state, one becomes intelligent, endowed with valor, esteemed, and sweet-spoken; such a person shall be wealthy and possessed of riches. || 4 ||
Constantly abandoned by his wife and distressed in mind,
he contemplates the meaning of all the scriptures when the fourth smoke-stage has arrived.
When Dhūma is situated in the fifth house, one has few offspring, is destitute of wealth,
eats everything indiscriminately due to the influence of Jupiter, and is deprived of friends and counsel.
If Dhūma is situated in the sixth house (the house of enemies), one becomes a powerful slayer of foes, endowed with great luster,
renowned, and always free from disease.
One born with Dhūma in the seventh house will always be destitute, constantly lustful, skilled in pursuing the wives of others, and forever devoid of luster.
Abandoned by valor, though full of energy and true to his promise,
he became unpleasant, cruel, and self-interested when death had entered the smoke.
When Dhūma is situated in the house of Dharma (the ninth house), one is endowed with the good fortune of sons, wealthy, honorable, compassionate, righteous, and affectionate toward kinsmen.

Endowed with the good fortune of learning, contented, wise, and happy, a man remains constantly established in his duty when the Moon is in the Dhūma yoga situated in the house of action (the tenth house). || 11 ||
When Dhūma is situated in the eleventh house, one becomes rich in wealth, grain, and gold, handsome, endowed with the arts, modest, and skilled in singing.

One who has fallen from his status, a doer of evil deeds, one addicted to the wives of others, one who is addicted to vices, merciless, and deceitful— these are the qualities associated with smoke for twelve years.
When a malefic planet has reached the ascendant, the native is afflicted by suffering;
he is cruel, murderous, foolish, and hateful toward his kinsmen. (14)

If the pāta-saṃjñaka [node] is situated in the second house, the person is crooked, afflicted with excessive bile, a seeker of enjoyments, merciless, ungrateful, evil-minded, and likewise a doer of sinful deeds. || 15 ||
When the Pāta of Saturn occurs in the third house, a man becomes firm in wisdom, fond of battle, a giver, wealthy, and a favorite of the king; he shall become a commander of an army. || 16 ||
When Pāta is situated in the fourth house, that person will be afflicted by bondage and disease, and deprived of sons and good fortune. || 17 ||
If Mars is in the fifth house, one is poor but endowed with beauty;
he is afflicted by phlegm, bile, and wind, and is cruel and shameless.
He is a slayer of enemies, well-nourished, and a master of all weapons;
he is skilled in the arts and tranquil when his enemy has fallen at his feet. (19)
Abandoned by wealth, wife, and sons, dominated by women, and filled with suffering; when Venus is in the seventh house, one is lustful, shameless, and devoted to others.
One with impaired eyes, deformed, unfortunate, and a reviler of the twice-born;
when Pāta is situated in the house of death, one is overwhelmed by suffering from blood.
One who has many undertakings, is always well-friended, and is highly learned;
when Venus is in the ninth house, he is fond of women and speaks pleasantly. (22)

He is endowed with splendor, a performer of dharma, and one who has reached the end of his duties; he is skilled in religious works, possessed of great wisdom, and discerning when the Moon is situated in the asterism known as Pātā.
When Pāta is in the eleventh house, one becomes possessed of abundant wealth, honorable, truthful, firm in vows, rich in horses, and devoted to song.

When Pāta is situated in the house of expenditure (the twelfth house), one is irascible, burdened with many undertakings, physically deformed, a defiler of righteousness, and a hater of one's own kinsmen. (25)
One born with Paridhi in the ascendant becomes learned, devoted to truth, peaceful, wealthy, possessed of sons, pure, charitable, and affectionate toward his teachers. (26)
A man born when Paridhi is situated in the second house becomes a lord, handsome, an enjoyer of pleasures, happy, devoted to righteousness, and a master of wealth. || 27 ||
In the third Paridhi, one is beloved by women, possesses a beautiful body, associates with gods and kinsmen, is a servant, and is endowed with devotion to his teacher.
If Paridhi is situated in the state of Sukha, it makes the enemy astonished and inauspicious;
however, if it is Sampūrṇa, it makes him free from cruelty and skilled in song.
One born under the fifth Paridhi is endowed with fortune, virtuous, handsome, beloved, and devoted to dharma; he becomes the favorite of women. (30)

If Paridhi is situated in the state of an enemy, a man is born who is distinguished, possessed of wealth and sons, an enjoyer of pleasures, devoted to the welfare of all beings, and a slayer of his foes. (31)

If the seventh house (the house of the wife) is situated in the *paridhi* yoga, one has few offspring, is devoid of happiness, possesses dull intellect, and is very harsh; furthermore, diseases of women arise.

One who contemplates the inner self, peaceful, firm of body, firm in vows, possessing the Dharma and endowed with courage, [should act] when the planet is situated in the cusp of the eighth house. 33.
Accompanied by sons, happy, beloved, wealthy, and free from greed; when Jupiter is in the ninth house, one is honorable and has a mind satisfied with even the slightest [gain]. (34)
Skilled in the arts, likewise an enjoyer of pleasures, firm of body, and free from envy, he reached the further shore of the meaning of all scriptures when the tenth year had arrived. || 35 ||
One born under the Paridhi yoga in the eleventh house becomes an enjoyer of women, virtuous, intelligent, and dear to his kinsmen; however, he is characterized by weak digestion.
If Mars is situated in the twelfth house, the person born there is always a spender of wealth;
he partakes in suffering, possesses a wicked intellect, and is devoted to censuring his elders. || 37 ||
When the Moon is in the sign of Sagittarius (Cāpa), a man becomes rich in wealth, grain, and gold, grateful, esteemed by the virtuous, and free from all defects. (38)
When the planet Saturn is situated in the second house, one is pleasant-spoken, endowed with boldness, humble, possessed of learning, handsome, and devoted to righteousness. (39)
If Sahaja is situated in the ninth house (Dhanus), one becomes miserly, highly skilled in the fine arts, always devoted to the act of theft,
physically deformed, and devoid of friendship.

When the Dhanus [ascendant] is situated in the fourth house, one becomes happy with cattle, wealth, grain, and so forth, honored and revered by the king; moreover, one becomes free from disease and possesses a well-formed body.
One born with Sagittarius in the fifth house is full of desire, far-sighted, devoted to the gods, pleasant-spoken, and excels in all undertakings.
When Sagittarius is situated in the sixth house, one becomes a slayer of enemies, exceedingly steadfast, happy, affectionate, pure, and a partaker in the success of all undertakings. (43)
When Saturn is situated in the seventh house, one becomes a lord, endowed with excellent qualities, learned in the scriptures, wise, and beloved; of this there is no doubt. (44)
One born when Sagittarius is situated in the eighth house becomes fond of others' work, cruel, devoted to the wives of others, and possesses deformed limbs. (45)
A man born when the moon is in Dhanuṣ, which is situated in Dharma, becomes an ascetic devoted to the practice of vows, preeminent in learning, and renowned throughout the world. (46)
One will possess many sons, wealth, and sovereignty, and own cattle, buffaloes, and other livestock; if the tenth house is conjoined with Sagittarius, one is born renowned throughout the world. (47)
When Venus is in the eleventh house, a man shall be endowed with gains;
he will be free from disease, possess a firm digestive fire, and be highly skilled in mantras, women, and weapons. 48.
One born when Saturn is situated in Sagittarius becomes a wicked person, excessively proud, evil-minded, and shameless;
being joined with another's wife, he is always destitute. (49)
Skilled in all branches of knowledge, happy, eloquent, and beloved,
one born when Śikhin is in the body will possess all desires.
When the banner (Jupiter) is situated in the house of wealth, one becomes an eloquent speaker, pleasant-voiced, and charming;
a composer of poetry, learned, honorable, humble, and endowed with vehicles.
When Ketu is situated in the third house, one becomes miserly, a doer of cruel deeds, emaciated in body, destitute of wealth, and afflicted by severe diseases. (52)
One who is handsome, endowed with virtues, sattvic, and fond of the Vedas,
always experiences happiness when the planet Jupiter is situated in a state of auspiciousness.

When Jupiter is situated in the fifth house, one becomes happy, an enjoyer of pleasures, skilled in the arts, knowledgeable in logic, intelligent, eloquent, and endowed with devotion to the guru. (54)
When the Dhvaja (flag) is situated in the sixth house, one causes the destruction of the maternal side, slays enemies, and possesses many kinsmen; he is brave, beloved, and wise. || 55 ||
One who is fond of gambling, lustful, and endowed with enjoyments;
when the banner (dhvaja) is situated in the seventh house, one forms friendships with courtesans. || 56 ||
Devoted to base actions, sinful, shameless, and always a reviler—he who had passed through three fortnights [of life] perished when the banner reached the place of death. (57)
Bearing the *liṅga*, with a serene soul, devoted to the welfare of all beings, he is skilled in religious duties when the auspicious time has arrived. (58)
O twice-born one, when Jupiter is situated in the tenth house, the native is endowed with happiness and good fortune, is beloved by women, is charitable, and is accompanied by Brahmins. (59)
He will have constant gains, be well-versed in the Dharma, honored when his gains are like fire, wealthy, fortunate, brave, a performer of excellent sacrifices, and exceedingly learned. (60)
When Ketu is situated in the twelfth house, a man becomes devoted to evil deeds, yet brave; he is devoid of faith, merciless, addicted to the wives of others, and fierce.
If Gulika is situated in the first house at birth, the person born will be constantly afflicted by disease, lustful, sinful-minded, deceitful, of wicked nature, and extremely miserable. (62)
When Gulika is situated in the second house at birth, the person becomes deformed, miserable, base, addicted to vices, shameless, and destitute of wealth. (63)
A man born with Gulika in the third house has beautiful limbs, is a village headman, is endowed with merit, is dear to virtuous people, and is honored by kings.
The sick person is always devoid of happiness and becomes a doer of evil;
if Gulika is situated in the house of happiness (the fourth house), he will suffer from an excess of wind and bile.
When Gulika is situated in the fifth house, one will be a panegyrist, a performer of rituals, short-lived, hateful, mean, and impotent;
he will be dominated by women and become an atheist.
One born when Saturn is in the house of enemies is free from foes, possesses well-nourished limbs, is highly radiant, esteemed by women, full of enthusiasm, very firm, and beneficial. (67)

When Gulika is situated in the seventh house, the native is conquered by women, is a doer of evil, is a paramour, has an emaciated body, and has lost his friends; he lives solely on the wealth of women.
When Gulika occupies its fallacy (randhra), one becomes hungry, miserable, cruel, intensely wrathful, and utterly merciless; such a person is born destitute and devoid of virtues.
One with many afflictions, emaciated body, evil deeds, and extreme cruelty; when Saturn is in Gulika and Jupiter is in the ninth house, he is a slanderer with a deceptive outward appearance.
One born when Gulika is in the tenth house will be accompanied by sons, happy, an enjoyer of pleasures, devoted to the worship of the gods and the sacred fire, and established in yoga and dharma.
When Gulika is situated in the eleventh house at birth, the person born becomes an enjoyer of excellent women, a ruler of subjects, devoted to the welfare of his kinsmen,
possesses limbs that are somewhat deficient, and becomes a sovereign emperor.
If Gulika is in the twelfth house, the person born is sinful, engaged in base occupations, deficient in limbs, unfortunate, and lazy; he finds delight among low-born people.
If the *prāṇapada* is in the ascendant, a person becomes ill at that moment;
he may be mute, insane, dull-limbed, deficient in limbs, miserable, or emaciated. (74)
When the vital breath (prāṇa) is situated in the house of wealth, a man is born fortunate, possessing abundant grain, abundant riches, many servants, and many offspring. (75)
If the *prāṇa-pada* is in the third house, one is violent, filled with pride, cruel, and an extreme thief; moreover, such a person is devoid of devotion to his teachers.

When Venus (Sukha) is situated there, he is happy; when Jupiter (Kānta), he is a beloved friend; when Mercury (Suhṛdramā), he is dear; when Saturn (Guru), he is devoted to his elders; when the Moon (Śīta), he is gentle; and when Mars (Prāṇa), he is indeed intent on truth.

One who possesses the *prāṇapada* in the fifth house becomes a partaker of happiness, endowed with virtuous deeds, compassionate toward those who have committed transgressions, and possessed of all desires. (78)
In the sixth *prāṇapada*, one is under the sway of kinsmen and enemies, sharp-tongued, having weak digestion, merciless, wicked, diseased, a consumer of wealth, and short-lived. (79)

A man who is constantly envious, lustful, and possesses a fierce and violent form, who is difficult to propitiate and possesses a wicked intellect, is found when the *prāṇapada* is situated in the seventh house. (80)
With his body tormented by disease when the eighth house is occupied by the lord of life (the Sun), he is afflicted by sufferings caused by kings and by death, kinsmen, and children. (81)

When the vital breath (prāṇa) is established in righteousness, one possesses sons, is endowed with wealth, is fortunate, and is pleasing to behold; likewise, a servant is always free from malice and wise.
He was energetic, wise, and skillful, an expert in the affairs of the king;
indeed, in his tenth stage of life, he was devoted to the worship of the gods.

When the vital breath (prāṇa) is situated in the house of gain (the second house), one is famous, virtuous, wise, an enjoyer of pleasures, endowed with wealth, fair-complexioned, and affectionate toward one's mother. (84)

A man born when [the Moon] is in Vyaya becomes base, wicked, deficient in limbs, and hostile toward those who are like brothers to the twice-born; or he is afflicted with eye disease or is one-eyed. (85)
Thus, O Brahmin, the results for the non-luminous planets have been stated;
likewise [those] for the luminous celestial wanderers, such as the Sun and others.
These [karmas] of embodied beings must be described according to their duration, according to the clarity of their manifestation, and by distinguishing between their strength and weakness. (87)
Now, the chapter on the calculation of the true aspects of the planets. || 26 ||
O Blessed One, how many kinds of views are there, and likewise, how many types of powers?
Such a doubt has arisen in me; you ought to resolve it. (1)

O twice-born one, that aspect previously mentioned as arising from the influence of the zodiacal sign (rāśi), and the other which arises from the inherent nature of the planet (kheṭa)—I shall now clearly explain that latter one. || 2 ||
In the third, the trine, the fourth, and the seventh house,
they aspect with increasing degrees of a quarter [of their full strength] and likewise bestow their results accordingly.
Furthermore, all [planets]—Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars—are fully [beneficial] in the seventh house;
moreover, they are especially so in the third, tenth, eleventh, ninth, fifth, and eighth houses.
Thus has it been explained in general by the former teachers;
and that vision which arises by virtue of the clear internal [perception] is exceedingly lucid, as follows.

Having subtracted the visible [longitude] from the observer [longitude], and having subtracted that difference exceeding six signs from ten signs, the degrees thereof divided by two shall be the true parallax. (6)

When [the result] exceeds five, the clear aspect (dṛk) is obtained from the division by the heap minus one; when it exceeds four, subtract the elements (five) from the division; when it exceeds three, the aspect is [obtained]. 7.

The result obtained by dividing the [remaining] ocean [four] by two, increased by thirty, is the *dṛk* (aspect). However, when [the remainder] is greater than two, it is the degrees [of the aspect], increased by the lunar days (*tithi*), excluding the sign (*rāśi*). (8)

O twice-born one, when Saturn is the observer and the remainder consists of signs and so forth, the aspect shall be obtained by dividing the degrees by two, even without a full sign. Thus it is when the remainder consists of signs and so forth.
In one sign, the elapsed and remaining degrees are doubled;
in two signs, they are diminished by half a degree; in eight signs, sixty; and in twelve signs, forty-five degrees. (10)

In the case of Mars, when there are twenty-one signs, sixty degrees minus the [longitude] portion (lavas) is added to fifteen degrees and a half; in two signs it is one degree, and in six signs it is always one degree. (11)
In the twenty-first [sign], the portion of Jupiter is thirty-five and a half;
in the twenty-fourth, it is sixty-two less by twice the number of degrees. (12)
In this way, the true aspect of the planets, beginning with the Sun, is produced;
by virtue of that alone, one should declare the results for the houses of the nativity. || 13 ||
Now begins the chapter on the clear strength (spaṣṭabala). || 27 ||

Now I shall describe the manifest strength (spaṣṭabala) arising from position, time, and other factors: one should subtract the planet, when it is below the horizon, from half the circle (180°), and if it is more than that, subtract it from the full circle (360°). || 1 ||
Having divided [the points] by nine and then divided by three, the result obtained shall be the exaltation strength (uccabala) in the following positions:
one's own trine, one's own house, the house of a great friend, the house of a friend, the house of a neutral, and the house of an enemy. (2)

And for those situated even in the house of the enemy, their strength [is calculated] in sequence as follows: five, four, three, two, one; zero, four, three, twenty, fifteen; fifteen, eight, ten, and four. (3)
In this manner, one should calculate the results arising from the hour (horā), decan (dṛkāṇa), ninth-part (navāṃśa), twelfth-part (dvādaśāṃśa), and thirtieth-part (triṃśāṃśa);
then, the sum of these constitutes the origin of the sevenfold division (saptavarga). || 4 ||
Venus and the Moon have full strength when in even signs, while others have strength equal to one-quarter in odd signs;
planets situated in the angles (kendras) and other houses have strengths of full, half, and one-quarter respectively.
Situated respectively in the decanates (dreṣkāṇas) at the beginning, middle, and end,
those known as male, neuter, and female bestow a strength equal to one-quarter [of a point].
From the Sun, Mars, Jupiter, Mercury, and Saturn, the fourth house is [calculated]; from the Ascendant and the Sun, the seventh;
and from Venus and the Moon, the tenth—provided that [the result] exceeds six signs. (7)
Having subtracted that from the circle [360°], its degrees are divided by three to obtain the strength of the direction.
The desired ghaṭīs from midnight constitute the *nata*; thirty subtracted from that is the *nata*.
The *nata* (ascensional difference) of the Moon, Mars, and Saturn, expressed in minutes and so forth, is doubled and subtracted from sixty; for the others, it is always one unit, except for Mercury.

Now I shall describe the strength of the lunar fortnights: having subtracted the moon from the sun, if [the remainder] exceeds six signs, one should subtract it from twelve signs; then, having divided by three, one should divide by three again. (10)

The strength arising from the fortnight for the Moon, Mercury, Venus, and Jupiter is obtained by subtracting sixty; the strength of the malefics arising from the fortnight is known by that same calculation. (11)
During the final third of the day, Mercury, the Sun, and Saturn possess full strength;
during the first third, the Moon, Venus, and Mars do so; and Jupiter always possesses full strength throughout.

The natural strength (naisargika-bala) previously stated for the lords of the year, month, day, lunar date (tithi), and the thirty divisions of the zodiac (carārṇava), as well as for the lord of the hour (hora), is sixty.
O twice-born one, sixty-seven times that measure, multiplied respectively by the numbers one and so on up to nine,
gives the [diameters] of the planets beginning with the Moon, Water, Gu (Jupiter), Śuci (Venus), and the Sun.
These [constants] are, respectively, five oceans (40), the gods (33), and the suns (12) as fractional parts;
and that [sum] is equal to the sum of the segments corresponding to the signs of the heliacal longitude of the planet. (15)
The degrees and so forth of the future [longitude] are increased by the quotient obtained from dividing [the elapsed time] by thirty;
these are positive or negative in the signs beginning with Libra and Aries respectively, and for Saturn and the Moon, they are added when the planet is in three signs [of its revolution]. (16)
Likewise, for Mars, the Sun, Jupiter, and Venus, the process is reversed; for Mercury, it is always wealth.
The degrees thereof, divided by three, should be known as the strength born of motion (āyanaja-bala). || 17 ||
Whatever is the solar strength and vigor known as *ceṣṭā* (activity), that indeed is the lunar strength of the fortnight (*pakṣabala*); to that same extent, it is remembered as *ceṣṭābala*. (18)
That [strength] is diminished by the aspect of malefic planets and likewise increased by the aspect of benefic planets;
when combined with the aspects of Jupiter and Saturn, it becomes the total strength of the planet. Thus shall the planetary strength be determined. (19)
Now, when two luminous planets are in mutual conflict, the difference in strength belongs to the victor as a positive quantity, while for the defeated one, it is a debt within their strength. (20)

The eightfold motion of the planets consists of: direct (cakra), retrograde (anuvakra), irregular (vikalā), slow (mandā), very slow (mandatarā), uniform (samā), swift (carā), and very swift (aticarā). || 21 ||
When moving retrograde, the strength is sixty; for one moving slightly retrograde, it is half;
for one with irregular motion, it is a quarter; and likewise for one moving at moderate speed, it is half.
For a planet moving slowly, the period is one quarter; for one moving more slowly still, it is half;
for one moving at a retrograde rate, it is three-quarters; and for one moving in accelerated motion (aticārin), it shall be half. (23)

The respective eccentric apogees, diminished by half the sum of the mean anomaly and the equation of the center, and reduced from the circle (360°) if exceeding six signs, are known as the anomaly centers (ceṣṭākendra) starting from Mars. (24)
Divided by three and the quotient obtained is called the "power of action" (ceṣṭābala).
Furthermore, there are six types [of strength]: arising from position, direction, time, aspect, action, and nature. (25)
Thus has the strength of the planets been declared; now hear the strength of the houses (bhāvas).
Virgo, Gemini, Libra, Aquarius, Sagittarius, and the first halves [of the signs] constitute the seventh [house]. (26)
One should abandon [the following] for the sake of happiness: from Taurus, Aries, Leo, Capricorn, and the first half of Sagittarius;
from Cancer and Scorpio, the Ascendant; and from the second half of Capricorn, Pisces, and Libra. (27)
The portion to be subtracted, being greater than six signs, is reduced by the zodiacal circle (twelve signs), divided, and multiplied by three;
it is then increased by one-quarter of a favorable aspect and decreased by one-quarter of a malefic aspect. || 28 ||
And that [house] should be conjoined with or aspected by benefics, and endowed with the strength of its own lord;
thus the clear general strength of the houses has been stated previously. (29)
The strength of a house conjoined with Mercury and Jupiter is increased by one;
the strength of a house devoid of Saturn, Venus, and the Sun is diminished by one. (30)

During the day, the state is one of rising from the front; at twilight, it is rising from both [front and back]; and at night, it is known as rising from the rear. These bestow a strength equal to one-quarter [of the total]. (31)
Nine, three, six, three, and four;
nine, three, thirty, and ten multiplied [by ten] respectively. (32)

O twice-born one, if there is a combination of the strengths of the Sun and the other planets, then they are considered very strong; if the strength is greater, it would indeed be full, and thus they are powerful.
O twice-born one, for Jupiter, Mercury, and the Sun, the values are six, five, and four; five, zero, and five; and zero, one, and one respectively. (34)

And the fires of the planets, in order, are established in place, direction, movement, time, and solstice: fifteen, one hundred and twenty-three, thirty-three, one hundred and twenty, and one hundred. (35)
O twice-born one, it is said that there are forty minutes for Mars and Saturn respectively; thirty, forty, forty-seven, and twenty for [Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Rahu]. 36.

O twice-born one, having thus performed the unification of the strengths, one should then consider the results arising from the planets situated in the houses and signs, according to the conjunctions previously described and the causes of those conjunctions. (37)
Among them, the one who is powerful is the agent, and he alone is the bestower of its fruit;
when many conjunctions have been attained, such is the proclaimed policy. (38)

One who is proficient in mathematics, who has exerted effort in the science of grammar, who knows logic, who is intelligent, who understands the directions, places, and times, and who has conquered his senses; || 39 ||
O Maitreya, he is skilled in reasoning and refutation, honored for his mastery of the *Horā* branch of astrology; if he speaks, his word shall surely be true—of this there is no doubt. (40)
Now begins the chapter on the calculation of the desired and undesired [results]. || 28 ||
Now, I shall describe the desired and undesired [effects] of the planets, by virtue of which they bestow the auspicious and inauspicious results of their periods (daśās). (1)
The planet situated in its own *nīca* (fall) should be subtracted from the circle of the zodiac (*bhamaṇḍala*) when it exceeds six signs;
that sign, increased by one, becomes the *ucca* (exaltation), joined with twice its degrees. || 2 ||
One should calculate its rays from the *ceṣṭākendra* (the point of maximum velocity) just as one calculates the rays of the exaltation;
O twice-born one, the *ceṣṭākendra* for Mars and the other planets has been previously described by me. (3)

The precession-corrected sun minus three signs is the *ceṣṭākendra* for the sun; likewise, the moon minus the sun is the *ceṣṭākendra* for the moon. If that [kendra] is less than six signs, it remains as is; if it exceeds six signs, it should be subtracted from the circle (twelve signs). || 4 ||
The half of the conjunction of the moving rays is proclaimed as the auspicious ray;
and that which is purified from the eight is called the inauspicious. || 5 ||
One should multiply the [planetary] longitudes, excluding the Sun, by ten and add one;
half of that result shall be known as "desirable" (iṣṭa), while sixty subtracted from it shall be "difficult" (kaṣṭa).
In its exaltation, its Mūlatrikoṇa, its own sign, its friendly sign, its neutral sign, its enemy sign, its great enemy sign, and its fall sign, respectively; || 7 ||
Sixty, four oceans (40), thirty, nine (39), fifteen (15), eight (8), four, two, and zero—this is the auspicious result for the house. (8)
If this remainder falls short of sixty, it is inauspicious in one's own house;
O Brahmin, half of that [remainder] should be known as auspicious or inauspicious in the other vargas.

In the first five [houses], there is a desirable result; in the sixth, it is equal; and beyond that, in the [remaining] three, it should be known as inauspicious—this is determined in the scriptures. (10)

The directional strength (digbala) and its directional result (dikphala), as well as the daily result (dinaphala), shall be determined; the result of these two is declared auspicious, while that which is diminished by sixty is inauspicious.

O twice-born one, when the auspicious [karmans] predominate, the result should be known as auspicious; when the inauspicious predominate, it is inauspicious. Such is the fruit of the planetary period (daśā) of a celestial body, and likewise the fruit of the house (bhāva).
Having combined the six strengths, one should divide by their total sum;
the resulting individual values shall be the respective strengths, both inauspicious and auspicious. (13)

One should destroy the aspect and likewise the strength by means of the results of the auspicious and the inauspicious; those two aspects are called auspicious and inauspicious, and the strengths shall be named accordingly. (14)

When the results of both the houses and their lords have been declared, if there is a benefic planet occupying the sign, then the results arising from the calculation of the house [are to be understood]. (15)

One should apply its fruit to what is auspicious and likewise avoid it in what is inauspicious; this applies if it is malefic, and similarly in the case of other planets, as well as in strength and aspect. (16)
One should apply the results when a planet is in its exaltation and the like, but discard them when it is in its fall and the like;
having thus understood the auspicious and inauspicious [influences], one should declare the results for the nativity. || 17 ||
The results of the eight groups (aṣṭavarga) are thus determined;
however, in the case of a house situated between two signs, the operation follows that of the lord of the sign [in which the house] is located. (18)
The attainment of a state is proclaimed to occur through a disposition that exceeds its own station;
and when that disposition is equal to it, one should then consider the planets as bestowing that station. (19)
Having added [the values] according to the number of places, this resulting figure is the fruit;
thus, the auspicious or inauspicious results for the houses along with their planets should be understood. || 20 ||
Now begins the chapter on words (padādhyāya). || 29 ||
O twice-born one, I shall now describe the positions of the planets and their specific results,
as previously declared by the great seers for the purpose of knowing them.
From the ascendant, in whichever sign the lord of the ascendant resides, the "pada" (position) of the ascendant is said to be in that manyth sign from the ascendant respectively. (2)
O twice-born one, the state of all existing things is likewise to be known as such;
therein, the wise recognize the state of the body as the primary state.
The seventh, *svasthāna*, cannot be a *pada* in this way;
when it is understood as a *pada*, it is to be known as the middle, the fourth *pada* in sequence.
Just as when the Lord resides in the fourth state, the fourth state itself becomes the plane;
so too, when the Lord resides in the seventh, the tenth plane is to be known.
O twice-born one, because the house from the planet is at whatever ordinal number [it may be],
they declare that the planet is mounted upon that same ordinal sign.
O Brahmin, having thus calculated the number of steps up to the limit of the strength for both the two lords and the two fears, one should then declare its result.
Then, O twice-born one, relying upon the *pada*, I shall describe some of its results when the eleventh house from the *pada* is conjoined with or aspected by planets. (8)
The child is born wealthy and likewise endowed with happiness;
through auspicious conjunctions, wealth is acquired by the right path, and likewise from sin.
When planets occupy their own, exaltation, friendly, or other such houses, the resulting fruit should be known as mixed;
gain arises in many ways, and the arrival of happiness occurs in many ways. (10)
If all the planets aspect the house of gain from the fourth house, he who is born there will become either a king or equal to a king; of this there is no doubt. || 11 ||
If one sees the house of gain from the foot [of the ascendant] and does not see any house of expenditure, O best of the twice-born, gain always arises without obstacle. (12)
O twice-born one, when there is an abundance of planetary aspects and conjunctions, and when [the planet] is in the eleventh house from the Pada,
or even if it is in an Argala, provided there is a gathering of many Argalas there as well.

O Brahmin, when there is a lock of benefic planets, and even more so when there is a lock of exalted planets, and it is aspected by a benefic lord, such as the lord of the ascendant or the ninth house; || 14 ||
One should indicate an increasing strength of fortune for the person born, provided that among the stated yogas, the planet does not aspect the twelfth house at all. (15)
O Brahmin, when the twelfth house from the *padasthāna* is conjoined with or aspected by both benefics and malefics,
there will always be an abundance of expenditure due to constant extraordinary acquisitions.

If a benefic planet is in its own path, [it brings] good results; if a malefic planet is on a wrong path, [it brings] evil; if they are mixed, a mixed result is to be declared; likewise, gain is also to be declared when [the planet] is in the eleventh house.
If Venus, the Sun, or Rāhu occupy the twelfth house from the ascendant, expenditure due to the king should be predicted, especially if there is the aspect of the Moon. || 18 ||

If Mercury is situated in the twelfth house from the Arudha Pada, conjoined with or aspected by benefic planets, there will be constant expenditure among kinsmen; however, if it is aspected by malefic planets, the expenditure results from quarrels.
O best of the twice-born, when Jupiter is in the twelfth house from the Pada and is aspected by other planets,
expenditure from one's own hand-roots (karamūla) must be declared.
O Brahmin, when Saturn has ascended the twelfth house and is conjoined with Mars,
and is aspected by other planets, there is expenditure of wealth due to one's circle of brothers.

Just as those yogas which have been described for when [the Moon] is situated in the twelfth house from the ascendant, those same yogas produce results of gain when [the Moon] is in the house of profit (the eleventh house). || 22 ||
If Rāhu or Ketu is situated in the seventh house from the ascendant,
the child suffers from abdominal pain or is afflicted by fire.
If Ketu is situated in the seventh house from the ascendant and is joined with or aspected by malefic planets,
the man will be impulsive, have white hair, and possess the characteristics of an old man.
But if Jupiter, Venus, and the Moon occupy the seventh house from the Pada, whether three, two, or even just one of them are present, the person born becomes possessed of fortune. (25)
O twice-born one, if a planet, whether auspicious or inauspicious, is in its own exaltation in the seventh house from the Pada,
that person will certainly become illustrious and endowed with noble fame.
O twice-born one, those yogas and the pādas that have been described by me in the seventh position must likewise always be considered in the second position as well.
Whether it be Rāhuṇeya (Venus), Jupiter, or indeed Venus itself, situated in its exaltation and occupying the second house, bestows prosperity upon the embodied being. || 28 ||

Those yogas which have been duly described by me for the ascendant (lagna) should also be understood to apply to the portion of the significator (kārakāṃśa), provided they are free from obstacles. || 29 ||
If a benefic planet is situated in the second house from the ascendant, one becomes the ruler of all lands;
furthermore, if it is Jupiter, he may become omniscient, and if Venus, a poet and an eloquent debater.

O twice-born one, when the house of the wife (the seventh house) is occupied by a planet situated in a quadrant or a trine, or when the houses of the ascendant and the wife are likewise conjoined with powerful planets, [the native obtains a wife]. || 31 ||
He will certainly become prosperous and indeed attain fame in his country;
however, one born with [Mars] in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house will be without wealth in matters of a wife.

If a planet possessing excellent strength is situated in the seventh house from the ascendant, or in its seventh, a quadrant, a trine, or the eleventh house, it bestows happiness upon both wife and husband.

Likewise, when [a planet] is situated in the seventh house from the foot, or in a quadrant or a trine, there will certainly be friendship between two [planets]; however, in the case of the three [houses], there is enmity, without a doubt. (34)
O Brahmin, in this manner, when the house of a son or others is situated from the house of the ascendant, the wise man should discern friends and enemies, as well as gain and loss. (35)

O Brahmin, if the lords of the ascendant and the seventh house are mutually situated in mutual quadrants, or in the third and eleventh houses, or in a trine, then the native becomes a king, a lord of the earth. (36)
O twice-born one, having thus examined both the house of the ascendant and the house of wealth and so forth, one should declare the results for the native. (37)
Now begins the chapter on secondary formations (upapada-adhyāya). || 30 ||
Now, O twice-born one, I shall describe the results based on the secondary signs (upapada):
the happiness arising from children, wife, and so forth that men may experience when [the Moon] is in the state of the Yoni. || 1 ||
O Brahmin, the state of the body is called the primary state;
that which arises from the attendants of the body is called the secondary state. || 2 ||
That very same term is known as the *upapada*, and likewise as the *gauṇapada*;
when that [term] is in the house of an auspicious planet and is conjoined with or aspected by a benefic planet. (3)
O best of the twice-born, full happiness regarding sons and wife arises when [the Moon] is joined with a malefic planet, situated in a malefic asterism, and aspected by a malefic. (4)
A man may become a renunciant or be deprived of his wife due to the conjunction with Śubhadṛk; however, this yoga does not cause the destruction of one's wife. || 5 ||
In this matter, the Sun would not be a malefic if it is situated in its exaltation, a friendly sign, or its own sign;
however, if it is situated in its fall or an enemy’s house, then it is indeed a malefic.
If there is the aspect of benefic planets upon the second house from the ascendant, and it is a benefic sign conjoined with a benefic, the previously mentioned result is indeed declared. || 7 ||
